newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: OAU opens way for Africans to seek top UN post.
newsitem.headline: OAU opens way for Africans to seek top UN post.

text.p: The chairman of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) has opened the way for another African to be elected U.N. secretary-general, urging African leaders to submit other names after the United States vetoed Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
This appeared to break a deadlock following the Nov. 19 U.S. veto when African states still seemed reluctant to put forward other candidates while Boutros-Ghali remained in play.

OAU Chairman Paul Biya said in a letter to African heads of state obtained by Reuters on Monday that it seemed time for African states wishing to do so to present other candidates jointly with that of Boutros-Ghali of Egypt.

Biya, the president of Cameroon, said this should be done to preserve Africa's chances of occupying the top U.N. post for a second five-year term. His letter, dated Nov. 29, said the countries concerned could inform the U.N. Security Council directly of their nominations while keeping him informed.

He called for speedy action in view of the urgency of the matter. Boutros-Ghali's term expires Dec. 31 and the United States has vowed to keep using its veto if necessary to deny him a second term on grounds the United Nations needs new leadership to carry out reforms.

Boutros-Ghali's immediate predecessors -- Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru, Kurt Waldheim of Austria and U Thant of Burma -- all had two five-year terms and this has become an unwritten U.N. tradition.

Biya noted that a July OAU summit in Yaounde, Cameroon, called for Africa to have a second term and recommended the re-election of Boutros-Ghali. But this did not succeed because of the veto by one of the Security Council's permanent members, he added.

Biya said that, according to his information, the 15-nation council appeared to favour a second term for Africa. A number of African diplomats have been mentioned as possible candidates but none has been formally submitted.
As recently as Monday, Ambassador Legwaila Joseph Legwail of Botswana, a Security Council member, told reporters: "We don't have any (new) list. It is composed of one person, Dr. Boutros-Ghali."

Among Africans mentioned as potential candidates are Under-Secretary-General Kofi Annan of Ghana, who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations; Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy; Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference; OAU secretary-general Salim A. Salim of Tanzania; Foreign Minister Moustapha Niasse of Senegal, and Olara Otunnu, a former Ugandan U.N. envoy who heads the New York-based International Peace Academy.
